title: Agent names: <repo>:<slug>:<role> for every process, with parentage
brief: Every process lyx spawns gets one hierarchical name (ly:landing:driver, ly:orch in the prime) as strand, Claude session and pane name, and records its parent; each repo gets a short code at fabric clone
body:
## Goal

Every process lyx spawns gets one hierarchical name, used as its strand name, its Claude session name and its pane title, and every worktree records its parent so questions go to the session that spawned it.
Delivery is Claude Code's own SendMessage; creel is deferred.

## Decided with the operator (2026-10-01/02)

- Full name `<repo>:<slug>:<role>`, e.g. `ly:landing:driver`; a process in the prime sits at the repo level and has no slug segment, so the hub is `ly:orch`.
  Two segments mean prime, three mean task.
  This replaces `process-naming`'s `<slug>:<role>[.<repo>]` grammar below.
- Several of one role: `-N` (`ly:orch-2`) or a free suffix (`ly:orch-design`); Discussion settles which.
- lyx writes the full name wherever something is addressed (Claude session name, `LYX_STRAND_NAME`, `LYX_PARENT`), so delivery is exact.
  People and agents write the short form (`orch`, `landing:driver`), read relative to their own repo.
- Every repo has a short code (`ly`, `mh`, `qu`).
  It is given at `lyx fabric clone` the first time a weft is bound, beside the warp URL, and recorded on weft:main next to the `.lyx-warp` binding and the lyx-anchor subpath, so later clones derive it.
  Existing hubs get it once through a fabric verb.
  Build the short code first: no name can be formed without it.
- No machine-wide slug check: fabric keeps slugs unique within a repo.
  Discussion settles whether lyx checks that two hubs on one machine do not share a short code.

## From reed-mailbox.md (naming part only)

From `manifest/designs/reed-mailbox.md`, which is otherwise deferred as the tier-3 note `creel`:

- Inject `LYX_STRAND_NAME` into every process reed spawns.
- The reed watchdog owns pane titles and Claude session names, restores them when they drift (Claude resets the session name after compact) and logs the drift.
- `lyx reed list` is the directory of names.

## From `process-naming`: Process naming and parentage: one name per process, the same in Claude messaging and creel

Operator 2026-09-30/10-01: a proper naming system so processes are easy to find, out of creel and general; one name per session and its strand (the hub, today ad hoc named lyxhub:orch, becomes loomyard:orch), usable both with Claude Code's built-in messaging, which already addresses sessions with a leading @, and with creel later, with the same syntax: two different addresses would be a mess. No @ inside names.
Grammar: `<slug>:<role>`, the shape the existing orchestrators already use ((quarry:orch, MH:orch)). The slug is always the worktree the process runs in; the hub orchestrator runs in the prime, whose slug is the repo name, so it is loomyard:orch (no special case; quarry:orch already follows this); role from a fixed vocabulary (orch, driver, worker, reviewer, operator) with an optional `-N` for several of one role. Slugs are [a-z][a-z0-9-]* and cannot contain `:`, so the split is unambiguous. Owned by one package. This supersedes the `name@slug[.hub]` grammar in manifest/designs/reed-mailbox.md (creel), which must use these names as its addresses; across repos creel uses the same name with an optional repo suffix, `<slug>:<role>[.<repo>]`, the suffix skippable when the repo is obvious (own repo); slugs and roles contain no `.`, so the suffix splits unambiguously. The Claude session name stays the short form: hub orchestrators are unique across repos anyway (the prime slug is the repo name), and a rare clash between two repos' worktree slugs is resolved by Claude's own [ref] disambiguation.
Mirrors: the strand name is a birth attribute in reed state, mirrored to the Claude session name (`claude --name`), the pane title (allow-set-title off) and `LYX_STRAND_NAME`; the reed watchdog restores drifted mirrors (Claude resets the session name after compact); `lyx reed list` is the directory.
Parentage: the spawner records `parent` (its own name) in the run seed at create time (batten run / loom start); every strand reed starts in that worktree gets `LYX_PARENT`; stencils tell agents that questions and notices go to `$LYX_PARENT`; no parent recorded means the operator (awaiting state). If the hub spawns a worktree, the hub is the parent of every process in it.
Delivery v1: Claude Code peer messaging (SendMessage to the parent's session name, used successfully 2026-09-30); creel replaces it later with the same names.
The hub sets its own name at session start or via lyx orch.
Prerequisite for orch-discussion-review's live question mode.

title: Discussion gets a partner: an answerer for its questions, the parent for review
brief: Discussion-Write either asks design questions of an answerer as they arise (ask: the parent or a dedicated agent spawned beside the writer) or drafts first and asks the parent for review (review, millhouse orch-review); the writer waits on files and always fixes
body:
## Goal

The parent (the session that spawned the run; the operator when none is recorded) takes part in Discussion through one of two modes, chosen per run; never both at once.

- **ask**: a running conversation.
  Discussion-Write asks its design questions as they arise, and the parent answers them; it is answers to design questions, not a review.
- **review** (millhouse's `orch-review`/`orch-wait`): Discussion-Write answers its own questions as best it can, finishes the draft, and then asks the parent for input; the parent's review comes back and the writer fixes it.

## Decided with the operator (2026-10-02)

- The parent answers every question; where writer and parent disagree, they argue it out in the files rather than either one deciding alone.
- The writer always fixes; there is no separate parent-review producer (a reviewing producer has no one to fix its review).
- Neither side's waiting may cost the parent its context:
  - The writer is a shuttle-run interactive session and waits on a file; shuttle keeps it non-terminal, as it already does for an asking session (`internal/shuttleengine/wait.go`), and a bound expires into `awaiting` with the open question or draft surfaced for the operator.
  - The parent arms a Monitor and, each round, forks a fresh one-shot agent that reads the exchange file, answers or reviews, and exits; no fork ever waits, so none is flagged dead by its master.
    A fork inherits the parent's context, and the exchange file records every answer with its reasoning, so continuity lives in those two, not in the fork.
  - A lyx verb delivers the parent's answer or review and wakes the writer.
- Rounds repeat until the parent approves or a round cap is reached; disagreement left at the cap becomes `awaiting` for the operator.
- The mode is a seed field set by the spawner (batten for hub runs); no parent means the operator, as today.
  Model it as two independent switches (`ask`, `review`) rather than one enum: one is on per run for now, but the operator sees both on later, served by two different agents, one answering the writer's interview questions and another doing the review (two agents designing together beat one agent asking and answering itself).
- Build the shared waiting first, then `review` (proven in millhouse), then `ask` on the same machinery.
- Later, not now: the same for Plan-Write.

## Verify early and live

- An idle interactive session in tmux is reliably woken by the delivering verb.
- The parent's Monitor-plus-fork loop costs little context per round (measure it on the first hub run).


## Who answers in ask mode (operator, 2026-10-02)

The answerer is an address, not hard-wired to `$LYX_PARENT`.
It can be the parent, or a dedicated agent spawned in parallel with Discussion-Write, with its own prompt: it studies the task and the code while the writer drafts, so it is ready when the questions come.
A dedicated answerer is a live session of its own, so the exchange is a real dialogue between two processes that both keep their context, and none of it lands in the parent's context.
That makes it the likely default for `ask`; the parent stays the natural `review` agent.
New machinery this needs: one producer running two interactive sessions side by side (writer and answerer, e.g. `ly:<slug>:discussion` and `ly:<slug>:advisor`), each waiting on the other through files.

## From `orch-discussion-review`: The orchestrator takes part in Discussion: questions to the parent and a review gate

Operator 2026-09-30/10-01: a weakness that the orchestrator is not involved in discussion; the hub must take part in the design.
Two mechanisms, built in this order:
1. Review gate (millhouse mill-start --orch with orch-review/orch-wait): a seed flag (batten sets it for hub runs) makes Discussion-Review round 1 an `awaiting` stop naming the discussion file; the parent is notified (message to $LYX_PARENT, with the hub's state watch as fallback); the hub forks a reviewer that writes the review in the review-output format (BLOCKING/NIT, class design/scope/decision/consistency, plus review-attack-surface's question) and records it with a verb in the approve/reject idiom; `lyx loom start` resumes; convergence needs two consecutive APPROVEs so round 1 alone never converges. File-based, so it survives a hub restart.
2. Live questions: where Discussion-Write would ask the operator interactively (as millhouse does), it sends each question to $LYX_PARENT and waits; the parent answers by message. shuttle already classifies an asking session (OutcomeAsking, AwaitOperator); route that to the parent instead of the operator. Needs process-naming (names and parentage). No parent or no answer within a bound: fall back to awaiting for the operator.
Open: the same for Plan-Review round 1.

title: PR-Rework as its own plan generation, design-reviewed
brief: Each rework round gets a fresh plan with only its own cards, so Webster never drags implemented cards along; rework cards that change a classifier, verb or guard go through Plan-Review
body:
## Goal

A PR-Rework round becomes a new plan generation: Webster sees only that round's cards plus `00-overview.md`, earlier cards are archived (git keeps them), and rework cards that add or change a classifier, verb or guard go through Plan-Review.
This is what made refusal-audit circle: four rework rounds grew its plan to 64 cards, of which 54 were done, which overflowed Master's launch prompt, let Master claim done with ten cards unrecorded, and exhausted the bounce budget.

## Also folded in

- `review-attack-surface`: the discussion and plan rubrics ask what a new verb or downgraded guard can skip or let through.
- `burler-focus-prior-round`: three refusal-audit friction notes hit the same ordering trap.
- refusal-audit self-report 5: Webster kept its earlier card list after rework; "Still to run" (`3613d5076`) patches the symptom, generations remove the cause.

## From `rework-design-review`: PR-Rework cards that change a classifier, verb or guard get a Plan-Review pass

loom-recipe.yaml:37 exempts PR-Rework from Plan-Review. Keep the exemption for text-only findings; route cards that create or change a classifier, verb or guard through Plan-Review.

### Rework should not drag the implemented plan along (operator, 2026-10-01)

PR-Rework appends its cards to the same plan, and Webster resumes the same run, so Master's prompt and context carry every earlier card's index and progress line.
In refusal-audit round 4 that was 64 batches with 54 done; the rendered prompt outgrew the launch limit (fixed on main in `e39909bbc` by handing Master the prompt as a file, which treats the symptom only).
Done cards are dead weight: Master never re-runs them, but they fill its context and every fork inherits it.
Want: each rework round is its own plan generation; Webster sees only that round's cards plus `00-overview.md`, and the earlier cards are archived (git keeps them), so prompt and context stay flat however many rounds a task takes.


## From `review-attack-surface`: Reviews ask what a new verb or downgraded guard can skip or let through

From a Fable process analysis of refusal-audit, 2026-10-01: Discussion-Burler round 1 F5 itself wrote "goto places no restriction on targets" (reviews/discussion/round-1-review.md:142); Plan-Review checks fidelity to the decision record and so cannot question it; Webster-Review reviewed the diff as code.
Want: loom-rubric-discussion-review.md (and the plan rubric) asks, for every new verb or downgraded guard, what it can now skip or let through; pairs with orch-discussion-review.

## From `burler-focus-prior-round`: Burler: round-N focus directive conflicts with the read-prior-rounds-last rule

Friction from run `operator-surface`, Burler Webster-Review round 2 (stencils from `d619100af`).
The round-2 focus directive asked the reviewer to check the round-1 F4 site list and the round-1 fix commits, which requires reading `round-1-review.md` and `round-1-fixer-report.md`.
The round prompt's instruction 2 says prior-round files are read only after the review is saved, so the focus file handed over in instruction 1 cannot be followed without breaking it; the reviewer read them early and said so.
Fix direction: the focus directive restates the sites it depends on, or the prior-round rule exempts what a focus directive names.

title: Verify localizes failures and Publish never runs on a dirty tree
brief: Cards verify with the integration tests and repo scans they touch, Publish never verifies or pushes a dirty tree, verify is never skipped after a crash, and every agent prompt goes through a file
body:
## Goal

A failing integration test stops on the card that caused it, Publish never verifies or pushes a dirty tree, and no gate is skipped after a crash.
refusal-audit stopped five times on integration-verify regressions that the plan-level verify could not localize.

## Also folded in, not in bolt before

- refusal-audit self-report 2: card `verify:` commands run package-scoped, so `cmd/lyx` repo-wide invariant scans first run at the plan level; Plan-Write could append `go test ./cmd/lyx/`.
- refusal-audit self-report 3: Webster's integration verify runs against the working tree, so an uncommitted edit can mask a non-compiling HEAD.
- Publish's conflict resolver reuses `.lyx/loom/conflict-resolution-r1.md` across Publishes (`internal/mergeresolve/spec.go:60`), so a later conflicting merge-in is refused while an earlier file exists; refusal-audit hit it.
- Deliver every agent prompt through a file, so no role can hit the 30000-byte launch limit (`internal/shuttleengine/claudeengine/command.go`); Master already does (`e39909bbc`).

## From `card-verify-integration`: Cards that touch integration-tagged tests verify with -tags integration

No refusal-audit card declared a verify: line; the fork gate is go build plus the package's unit tests (webster-body-implementer.md:30), untagged, while 11 of 48 touched test files are //go:build integration.
Want: Plan-Write adds `go test -tags integration <pkg>` to a card's verify when it touches a tagged file; a message-rewording card greps the repo for the old text first so stale exact-string assertions become part of the card; Master re-runs integration tests after a rework fork.

## From `publish-dirty-tree`: Publish must not verify or push a dirty tree after merge resolution

refusal-audit's Publish merge left historyfold_test.go uncommitted and verify ran on the dirty tree; earlier publish-review-fixback had the same uncommitted merge-resolution edits

## From `verify-gate-crash-after-merge`: Landing verify gate skips a merge interrupted before its marker write

Found reviewing PR #308 (`publish-verify-after-merge`).
Fabric reports a finished-but-interrupted merge as already up to date, so the gate cannot tell a verified tree from an unverified one.
Robust fix: record the task HEAD that last passed verify, and verify whenever HEAD differs from it.

title: Clean pair lifecycle: no leftover sessions, branches, sockets or races
brief: fabric remove ends the pair's tmux session, finishes half-removed pairs and deletes warp branches on origin; loom start never races a dying driver; tests stop leaking tmux sockets
body:
## Goal

Removing a pair ends its tmux session first, can finish a half-removed pair, and leaves no branches, sockets or stray directories behind; starting a run never races a dying driver.

## Also folded in, not in bolt before

- After refusal-audit landed, the driver wrote a drive report into the weft; `lyx fabric remove --remote` removed the task worktree, refused the dirty weft, and a rerun answered "worktree not found", so the half-removed pair had to be finished by hand.
- Warp branches on origin (see `fabric-branch-hygiene` below): `remove --remote` deletes the weft branch on origin but never the warp branch, and squash merges mean git never sees them as merged.
  On 2026-10-02 the hub deleted 37 such warp branches by hand (no open PR, no live pair).
  Want: `remove --remote` deletes the warp branch on origin too, and `fabric cleanup --remote` finds warp branches on origin with no live pair and no open PR.

## From `fabric-remove-ends-reed-session`: fabric remove leaves the pair tmux session alive

Seen 2026-09-30 for quarry-cli-answers and status-strand-by-driver: after landing and `fabric remove --remote`, their reed sessions were still alive hours later.
A driver that wrote its stop report after the removal recreated `<hub>/<slug>/.lyx/...` and `<hub>/<slug>/_lyx/shed/<slug>/drive-reports/<report>.md`: a stray directory, and a drive report that never reached the archive.
The hub killed the sessions and deleted the dirs by hand.

Fix: remove (and batten teardown) ends the pair reed session (reed down) before deleting the worktrees, and waits for or refuses on a live driver; a stop report written after done should land before the archive tag.

## From `driver-restart-race`: loom start races the ly-drive self-removal and ends with no driver

After a hand-back, the ly-drive session removes its own strand with a detached `lyx reed remove --name loom-driver --detach` that waits for the session's pid to exit (end-of-session command from `083e992cf`).
A `lyx loom start` issued in that window sees the loom-driver strand still live, keeps it instead of spawning a driver, and the detached remover then deletes it: the run is left with no driver and nothing happens (hit on `batten-hub-ready` and `focus-marker-warn`, 2026-09-30; a second `loom start` works).
Fix direction: `loom start` treats a driver strand with a pending self-removal (or whose claude has exited) as gone and spawns a fresh one, or the remover skips a strand that was re-adopted since it was scheduled.

## From `batten-resume-sees-stale-blocked`: batten run right after loom start exits on the child's stale blocked state

Seen 2026-09-30 on batten-records-leak-into-pairs: after a hub fix, `lyx loom start --no-attach` (ok) followed at once by `lyx batten run` ended with Run-Shed "inner shed run reached state blocked" because status.json still said blocked for a few seconds.
Fix direction: loom start writes state running (or a resume marker) before returning, or batten treats a blocked child whose driver was just relaunched as running.

## From `fabric-branch-hygiene`: Fabric: branches left behind by a failed add and on the remote

Read the closed GitHub issues #269 (add rollback leaves the warp branch) and #270 (cleanup cannot see weft branches stranded on the remote). Re-check both once `landing` has landed: it takes #293 (remove leaves the warp branch, locally and on origin), which touches the same branch-lifecycle code, and the ly-drive may repair the rest from a trace.

After `landing` (#298): `fabric remove` now deletes the local warp branch, but `--remote` still deletes only the weft branch on origin; warp branches of removed pairs stay there (`board-done-on-landing`, `burler-exclude-warn`, `integration-verify-fence`, `loom-start-layout`, `stencil-drift-remedy`, `stuck-reason-in-status`, `landing`). Out of scope in landing's decision record.

## From `main-weft-not-pushed`: main-weft is never pushed and never advances on landing

Seen 2026-09-30, uninvestigated: the prime weft branch main-weft stays local and does not move when a task lands

## From `test-tmux-socket-leak`: Integration tests leave tmux sockets behind

Tests leak tmux sockets: `/tmp/tmux-1000/` holds hundreds of `lyx-Test…`, `lyx-contract-…` and `lyx-warp-bare-…` sockets left by reed/loom integration tests. Test fixtures should kill their tmux server and remove the socket in `t.Cleanup`.

title: PATTERN for loomyard, plus repo conventions
brief: CONSTRAINTS.md becomes _lyx/PATTERN.md so agents get the constraints directive; warp/weft scan beyond Go code; model specs in short form; ide workspace cleanups
body:
## Goal

loomyard gets `_lyx/PATTERN.md` so lyx agents receive the constraints directive, which no run has received so far; CONSTRAINTS.md moves there.
Runs alone, last: it repoints CONSTRAINTS.md in ~130 files.

## Also folded in

- `fabric-vocabulary-everywhere`, `model-spec-short-form` and `ide-hub-workspace-followups` below.
- `model-spec-short-form`'s model trial (`fable[high]` for discussion and review) moved to `convergence-plan`, where it is measured; this task does only the short form, the dead link and Master's explicit effort.

## From `pattern-init`: Initialize PATTERN for loomyard: CONSTRAINTS.md becomes _lyx/PATTERN.md

Operator 2026-10-01: CONSTRAINTS.md is millhouse's setup; loomyard's variant is PATTERN, not yet initialized.
Verified: no _lyx/PATTERN.md in loomyard-weft, and there is no init verb. internal/pattern injects a role directive (implementer, review-fix, orchestrator) pointing at _lyx/PATTERN.md into webster fork/Master, burler and loom plan prompts only when the file exists, so today's runs got no PATTERN directive (they only saw CONSTRAINTS.md through CLAUDE.md and stencil mentions).
Work: move CONSTRAINTS.md's invariants into _lyx/PATTERN.md (weft, invisible to the code repo; optionally split under _lyx/pattern/); repoint everything that names CONSTRAINTS.md: CLAUDE.md, stencils (loom discussion/plan/rework, webster master and prefix-recovery), the ly-drive skill, contracts/specs, burlercli/run.go, loomshed and treadleengine docs, and contracts/stencils/citation_enforcement_test.go; decide whether a `lyx pattern init` verb is wanted for other repos.

## From `fabric-vocabulary-everywhere`: Fabric vocabulary: warp and weft only inside fabric, also in docs, specs and tests

Operator 2026-09-30: warp and weft are fabric-internal words; nothing outside fabric should know them.
Seen on refusal-audit: contracts/specs/refusal-spec.md and several _test.go files outside fabric use them, and the scan let them through.
Want: extend the scan to contracts/, docs/, manifest/, plugins/ skills and test files outside the owner set (or an explicit allowlist for fabric docs), and sweep the existing hits.

## From `model-spec-short-form`: Model specs in the short form everywhere, and per-role model choice revisited

Seen 2026-10-01: long form in internal/loomengine/template.yaml (discussion, plan, review, friction), internal/websterengine/template.yaml (recovery), internal/landingshed/template.yaml (conflict, describe) and contracts/specs/llm-model-spec.md's examples; the spec only mentions in one sentence that a bare bracket token means effort. Template comments cite docs/reference/model-spec.md, which is missing; the spec lives at contracts/specs/llm-model-spec.md.
Webster master is plain `sonnet`, so its effort (medium) comes invisibly from models.yaml; write it explicitly.
Model choice (operator, 2026-10-01): try `fable[high]` for discussion and review, where design judgement matters (refusal-audit's holes came from opus Discussion and opus reviews; a Fable review found the design problem), keep sonnet for implementation; change it only between runs and measure review rounds, PR rejects and interventions before and after (convergence-plan).

## From `ide-hub-workspace-followups`: ide hub workspace: review follow-ups

Follow-ups from the PR #301 review (`85902381e`), all non-blocking:
- `internal/fabricengine/hubworkspace.go` builds the prime path by hand (`filepath.Join(l.HubPath, primeName, l.AnchorRel)`) instead of `WorktreePath`.
- `internal/ideengine/spawn.go` now WARNs on every spawn whose prime resolution fails, task spawns included (silent before).
- Removing the last pair prunes `_portals/<anchor>`, so the hub workspace shows a missing folder until the next prime spawn.
- Relative-path settings spliced from the prime into the workspace file resolve against `_launchers/`, not the prime.

title: Bolt as the roadmap, manifest/ retired
brief: One entry store with a numeric tier and a type, a README rendered like roadmap.md, lyx board find and a compact listing; then manifest/ is deleted after its durable content moves to package docs
body:
## Goal

Bolt becomes the roadmap: one store with a numeric tier and a `type`, a README rendered like roadmap.md, `lyx board find`, a compact listing; then `manifest/` is deleted.

## manifest/ retirement

The triage was done in the bolt review of 2026-10-01/02; what survives is already in bolt.
This task moves the durable reference content into package docs, fixes inbound links and deletes the folder (Millhouse has no ownership of `manifest/`).

- `manifest/HANDOFF.md`: the hub run loop goes to the `internal/orchcli` package doc; the rest is spent.
- `hardener.md`: the text-review vs behaviour-review distinction and the respawn rationale go to `internal/treadleengine`'s doc.
- `fabric-windows-verification.md`: the Linux-only caveat goes to the `internal/fabricengine` and `internal/fslink` docs.
- `webster-parallel-execution.md`: the 42-card case study and the index-race rationale go to `internal/websterengine`'s doc.
- `review-finding-classification.md`: the convergence case study goes to `internal/burlerengine`'s doc.
- `curation-triage.md`: one line in the boardengine doc ("anyone adds notes, the orchestrator curates"); the automation is struck.
- Inbound links: `internal/treadleengine/doc.go`, `internal/fabricengine/livestate_doc_test.go`, `contracts/specs/loom-plan-spec.md`, `docs/overview.md` (lifecycle text and design links), `crucible/README.md`, `crucible/review-prompt-template.md`, CLAUDE.md's Task completion rule, `.claude/agents/mill-done-gate-fixer.md`.

## From `bolt-roadmap-tiers`: Bolt as the roadmap: three numbered tiers in one store, rendered like roadmap.md

### Why

Operator 2026-10-01: `manifest/roadmap.md` is very readable and bolt's README is not.
Bolt should follow the roadmap's principle; everything in it matters to the orchestrator, since the future direction shapes how Planned work is reviewed.

### Tiers

1. Concretized and claimable (rendered Planned).
2. Planned next but not concretized; not claimable until promoted (Next Up).
3. Loose ideas the operator has thought about, as in roadmap.md today (Someday).

### Storage

- One store, not `tasks.json` + `notes.json` (and not three files); every entry carries a numeric `tier`.
- The data holds only the number; the renderer alone owns the section names.
- Claimable means tier 1; promotion lowers the number (3 → 2 → 1, skipping allowed); new ideas default to tier 3.
- The task and notes verb groups collapse onto it; migrate the two existing files.
- Operator also wants a `type` field (e.g. design, bug, idea, chore) alongside the tier; settle the type set in Discussion.

### Rendering

- README like roadmap.md: one section per tier, in tier order, each with a one-line meaning.
- One `1.` item per entry with **title**, slug, one or two what/why sentences and the design link; no per-entry headings, no numeric ids.
- Optionally live state, producer and PR on running tier-1 entries.
- Design docs render as markdown: today a body written with single newlines shows as one paragraph.

### Agent ergonomics (folded in from `board-agent-ergonomics`)

The hub fell back to jq on `notes.json` because `lyx board list` shows tasks only and nothing searches.

- `lyx board find <text>` over every entry.
- A compact human listing (tier, slug, title) besides the JSON.
- The `get`/`remove` payload shapes in `--help`.
- A skill or doc telling agents how to use bolt (see also `lyx-mcp`).

### Also folds in

- `board-prune-done`: one verb removing every done entry, its design doc and dangling `depends_on`.
- After the manifest triage, roadmap.md's Someday moves into bolt and bolt becomes the only roadmap (`manifest-to-bolt`).
- Content job, not code: rewrite entry briefs as what/why during the review.


## From `manifest-to-bolt`: Move everything in manifest/ into bolt and retire the folder

Operator 2026-10-01: LYXHUB takes over all development of loomyard; everything in manifest/ goes into bolt.
The operator also says much of it is outdated: triage each roadmap Someday item with the operator (keep as tier 3 or tier 2, merge, or strike) and carry its designs/<name>.md over as the bolt entry's design doc.
Depends on bolt-roadmap-tiers for the tiers and the readable render.
Afterwards: delete manifest/, and update CLAUDE.md (Task completion section names manifest/roadmap.md and manifest/designs/), docs/overview.md's Documentation Lifecycle and any stencil or test that names manifest/.
